title: Audit Export — S3 Delivery Testing Matrix (beta)
content:
Context / goal
- This is the working test matrix for the S3 destination adapter used by SIEM-ready audit export beta.
- Focus: IAM + bucket policy patterns, encryption (SSE-S3/SSE-KMS), KMS key policy edge cases, cross-account assume-role, multipart upload behavior, and failure injection.
- Delivery semantics reminder: exporter is at-least-once; customer-side dedup should use audit.event_id. “Missing events” often equals lag + backfill behavior.

Assumptions about current implementation (as of PR-1068)
- Objects are written to customer-provided bucket/prefix.
- Format: newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) of canonical audit events (schema v2). Gzip compression may be enabled by config.
- Partitioning: prefix includes tenant/workspace and date/hour shards (exact path can change; treat as opaque except for prefix root).
- Checkpointing: exporter persists last successful checkpoint per {tenant, destination}.
- Multipart upload: used when payload exceeds threshold (verify threshold in config; test both below/above).
- Cross-account: exporter can assume customer role via STS; ExternalId supported/required by default for cross-account.

How to run tests (quick)
1) Provision bucket + role + kms per scenario.
2) Create destination in control plane (feature-flag tenant allowlist must be enabled).
3) Trigger audit events (synthetic generator or real admin actions) and wait for exporter to deliver.
4) Validate:
   - S3: object exists, encryption headers match expectation, content parseable, no prohibited/PII fields.
   - Exporter metrics: success count increments; error counters match injected failures; lag within expected.
5) For failure injection: run for ~15–30m to observe retries/backoff; ensure no hot loop; ensure DLQ behavior (if applicable to adapter/batch).

Legend
- Sev: P0 blocks beta / P1 must-fix / P2 acceptable limitation with docs
- Expected exporter behavior: retry w/ backoff, pause destination, DLQ batch, or surface config validation error.
- “Config validation error” = reject config at create/update time (control plane) OR disable destination at sync time.


A) Baseline / happy path scenarios
| ID | Scenario | Setup (bucket/role/kms) | Steps | Expected result | Sev | Notes |
|----|----------|--------------------------|-------|-----------------|-----|------|
| A1 | Same-account, SSE-S3 | Bucket in same AWS account as exporter role; default S3 encryption (AES256) | Create destination; emit 100 events | Objects delivered; ServerSideEncryption=AES256 | P0 | Baseline sanity check |
| A2 | Same-account, SSE-KMS (AWS-managed key) | Bucket default encryption = aws/s3 | Create destination with SSE-KMS enabled (if supported) | Objects delivered; SSE-KMS, key=aws/s3 | P0 | If config doesn’t allow selecting aws-managed key, document limitation |
| A3 | Same-account, SSE-KMS (customer-managed CMK) | Bucket default encryption = CMK; exporter role has kms:Encrypt/GenerateDataKey | Emit events | Objects delivered; SSE-KMS w/ CMK; no AccessDenied | P0 | Validate key policy includes exporter principal |
| A4 | Prefix isolation | Bucket shared by customer; distinct prefix per workspace | Configure two destinations (different prefixes) | No writes outside prefix; least-privilege policy works | P0 | Confirms we can scope IAM to prefix |
| A5 | Large batch triggers multipart | Lower multipart threshold (test env) or generate large payload | Emit enough events to exceed threshold | Multipart upload completes; object is readable; checkpoint advances | P0 | Ensure aborts are handled on failure |


B) IAM policy / bucket policy patterns
| ID | Scenario | Setup | Steps | Expected result | Sev | Notes |
|----|----------|-------|-------|-----------------|-----|------|
| B1 | Minimal same-account IAM (PutObject only) | Role policy: s3:PutObject to arn:aws:s3:::bucket/prefix/* | Emit events | Success; no need for ListBucket (unless adapter requires) | P0 | If ListBucket required for validation, call out and document |
| B2 | Bucket policy requires TLS | Bucket policy denies aws:SecureTransport=false | Emit events | Success (SDK uses TLS) | P1 | Regression guard |
| B3 | Bucket policy requires specific encryption | Bucket policy denies PutObject unless SSE-KMS | Configure SSE-S3 destination | Delivery fails with clear error surfaced; SSE-KMS config succeeds | P0 | Clear operator message needed |
| B4 | Bucket policy denies incorrect prefix | Bucket policy allows PutObject only to prefix A; config uses prefix B | Create destination; emit | Fails; surfaced as AccessDenied; no writes | P0 | Ensure error includes bucket+prefix (no secrets) |
| B5 | Missing s3:AbortMultipartUpload permissions | Role lacks AbortMultipartUpload | Force multipart then inject failure mid-upload | Exporter should handle/clean up; if it can’t abort, surface as known limitation | P1 | Track costs/garbage objects |
| B6 | Role permission boundary blocks KMS | Role has boundary denying kms:GenerateDataKey | Enable SSE-KMS | Delivery fails; clear error; no repeated hot loop | P0 | Common enterprise misconfig |


C) Cross-account assume-role
| ID | Scenario | Setup | Steps | Expected result | Sev | Notes |
|----|----------|-------|-------|-----------------|-----|------|
| C1 | Cross-account role w/ ExternalId required | Customer creates role trust to exporter acct with sts:ExternalId | Configure destination with role_arn + external_id | Success; CloudTrail shows AssumeRole; S3 objects delivered | P0 | ExternalId must not be logged |
| C2 | ExternalId mismatch | Wrong external_id in destination | Emit events | Destination enters error; retries w/backoff; clear “AssumeRole failed” reason | P0 | Ensure we don’t leak expected ExternalId |
| C3 | Trust policy missing exporter principal | Customer role trust doesn’t include exporter | Emit | AssumeRole AccessDenied; surface guidance | P0 | Provide snippet in docs (internal + customer) |
| C4 | Cross-account + CMK in bucket account | Bucket + KMS CMK in customer account | Emit | Success only if KMS key policy allows assumed role; otherwise fail with KMS AccessDenied | P0 | Validate key policy patterns below |
| C5 | STS regional endpoint constraints | Customer requires sts.<region>.amazonaws.com | Run in non-default region test env | Success OR documented limitation | P2 | Only if we currently hardcode global STS in some env |


D) KMS key policy / encryption edge cases
| ID | Scenario | Setup | Steps | Expected result | Sev | Notes |
|----|----------|-------|-------|-----------------|-----|------|
| D1 | CMK policy allows S3 but not exporter role | Key policy only allows s3.amazonaws.com via bucket encryption | Emit | If S3 performs encryption on behalf, it may still fail; verify actual required permissions | P0 | This one is subtle; record findings per AWS behavior |
| D2 | CMK disabled / pending deletion | Disable key or schedule deletion | Emit | Delivery fails; exporter backs off; status shows KMS error | P0 | Ensure paging/alerts if widespread |
| D3 | Wrong KMS key ID/ARN in config | If config supports explicit key id | Emit | Config validation error (preferred) or runtime failure; no partial writes | P1 | Avoid repeated retries with obviously invalid key |
| D4 | KMS key in different region | Bucket in us-east-1, key in us-west-2 | Emit | Validation error or runtime error; documented | P1 | Prefer validation |
| D5 | Customer requires bucket key (S3 Bucket Keys) | Enable bucket key on SSE-KMS bucket | Emit | Success; no compatibility issues | P2 | Mostly “should just work” |


E) Multipart upload behavior
| ID | Scenario | Setup | Steps | Expected result | Sev | Notes |
|----|----------|-------|-------|-----------------|-----|------|
| E1 | Multipart success path | Large payload | Emit until multipart | Complete upload; object decrypts; content intact | P0 | Validate gzip integrity |
| E2 | Network timeout during part upload | Inject timeout mid-part (toxiproxy) | Run for 20m | Retry part upload; eventually succeed; no duplicate checkpoints | P0 | Check that checkpoint only advances on complete |
| E3 | 5xx from S3 during CompleteMultipartUpload | Fault injection: return 500 | Run | Retry complete; if uncertain state, verify idempotency behavior (may create duplicate objects) | P0 | If duplicates possible, ensure naming strategy prevents overwriting |
| E4 | Partial multipart left behind | Kill exporter during multipart | Restart | On restart, no crash loop; leftover multipart either cleaned up or tolerated | P1 | Consider lifecycle cleanup policy |
| E5 | Multipart with SSE-KMS | SSE-KMS bucket + large payload | Emit | Success | P0 | Ensure encryption headers propagate on multipart |


F) Failure injection / negative tests (runtime)
| ID | Scenario | Injection | Steps | Expected result | Sev | Notes |
|----|----------|----------|-------|-----------------|-----|------|
| F1 | AccessDenied on PutObject | Remove PutObject permission after success | Observe exporter | Destination errors; retries with exponential backoff; status endpoint shows last error; no crash | P0 | Should be obvious to customer |
| F2 | Bucket not found | Configure wrong bucket name | Emit | Config validation error preferred; otherwise runtime fail with clear error | P1 | Avoid leaking internal AWS account info |
| F3 | Wrong region (PermanentRedirect) | Bucket in region A; client uses region B | Emit | Adapter follows redirect or errors with actionable message | P1 | If we don’t follow redirects, document |
| F4 | Throttling (SlowDown / 503) | Inject S3 throttling | Emit sustained load | Backoff; export lag increases but bounded; no noisy looping | P0 | Confirm max lag safety behavior |
| F5 | Destination pause behavior | Force repeated failures (e.g., AccessDenied) | Observe for 1h | After threshold, destination auto-pauses (if implemented) and surfaces guidance | P1 | Align with SRE runbook/alerting |
| F6 | KMS AccessDenied | Remove kms permissions | Emit | Fail with KMS-specific error; no plaintext fallback | P0 | Must not silently downgrade encryption |
| F7 | Large backlog + recovery | Stop outbound (deny policy) for 2h then restore | Emit during outage | Backfill catches up; checkpointing correct; no gaps beyond retention/backfill window | P0 | Track time-to-catch-up |
| F8 | Object content redaction check | Include known sensitive inputs that should be redacted (per policy) | Emit (synthetic) | Exported event does not contain prohibited fields; redactions applied | P0 | Coordinate with Security on canonical tests |


G) Customer-config “gotchas” to document (as we learn)
- CMK policy must allow the assumed role principal (not just the S3 service) depending on how encryption is requested.
- Prefix scoping is strongly recommended; don’t grant PutObject to bucket root.
- ExternalId required for cross-account; mismatches show up as AssumeRole AccessDenied.
- Multipart failures can leave incomplete uploads unless we explicitly abort; customers may want an S3 lifecycle rule to expire incomplete multipart uploads.


Validation checklist (per run)
- S3 object headers:
  - ServerSideEncryption = AES256 OR aws:kms
  - SSEKMSKeyId matches expected (if visible)
- Content:
  - NDJSON parses
  - Required fields present: event_id, timestamp, tenant/workspace identifiers, actor, action, resource
  - No disallowed payloads/PII per audit redaction policy
- Exporter telemetry:
  - Success counters increase
  - Retry counters match failure injection
  - Export lag returns to baseline after recovery
  - No high-cardinality labels introduced (sanity check dashboards)

Open questions / TODO
- Do we require s3:ListBucket for any health check / “test connection” flow? If yes, keep it optional and clearly requested in UI with rationale.
- Confirm if adapter writes one object per batch or uses time-based rollups; update matrix expectations accordingly.
- Decide whether to validate bucket region at config time (control plane) vs runtime (adapter).
- Confirm behavior on “uncertain complete” multipart (client timeout after CompleteMultipartUpload). Need deterministic object naming to avoid duplicates or safe overwrite strategy.

Change log
- 2025-04-29 (Diego): Added cross-account + CMK scenarios (C4, D1) and multipart failure injections (E3/E4).
- 2025-04-18 (Hanae): Added KMS boundary and disabled key cases (B6, D2).
- 2025-03-28 (Leila): Added backlog + recovery scenario (F7) aligned with backpressure controls.
